newsitem.title: USA: Cold spell to boost US NE energy use Fri-Mon - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Cold spell to boost US NE energy use Fri-Mon - WSC.

text.p: Energy demand for heating in the U.S. northeast, the world's biggest heating oil market, will rise to above to well above normal levels over the next few days, private forecaster Weather Services Corp (WSC) said.
Temperatures in the U.S. northeast will average 5-10 degrees Fahrenheit above normal on Thursday, cooling to 4-8 below normal on Friday, 5-10 below normal on Saturday and 3-6 below normal on Sunday.
Energy usage for heating in the area will average below normal on Thursday, much above normal Friday-Sunday, above normal on Monday and near to above normal on Tuesday.
Energy usage for heating in the U.S. Midwest will average much above normal Thursday-Saturday, above normal on Sunday, near to below normal on Monday and below normal on Tuesday.

Energy usage for heating in Europe will average below normal in the west and north, near to above normal in the interior, through to Friday. It will decrease on Saturday and Sunday, before increasing again next week, WSC said.
